text: March 15th, 44 BC. Julius Caesar is stabbed.
He sees his friend Brutus and gasps: "Et tu, Brute?"
Nope. Probably not.
Caesar's last words: the Shakespeare myth.
That line comes from Shakespeare's play.
Written in 1599. Over 1,600 years later.
So what did the Roman writers say?
Suetonius says Caesar said nothing at all. Just a groan.
But he adds that some people told a different story.
That Caesar spoke in Greek: "You too, child?"
Rich Romans often spoke Greek. It was fancy.
Plutarch says when Caesar saw Brutus, he just covered his head with his toga.
He was stabbed 23 times.
A doctor said only one wound was deadly.
So where does the Latin line come from?
It shows up in English plays before Shakespeare, as well.
Shakespeare just made it famous.
Caesar's real last words? Nobody knows.
Proof Caesar ever said it: zero.
Anyway, here's Caesar. "Et tu, Brute?"
